project_metadata.package_name: VOID: The Unseen Hand — Gameplay Package
project_metadata.author: VOID Gameplay Systems Architecture

upstream_dependency.role: World geometry, districts, registries, and streaming architecture only.
upstream_dependency.modification_policy: This package never modifies, recreates, or duplicates Meridian_Master content. It may reference Meridian_Master registries by ID (e.g. district IDs, tracked state variable names) but treats every such reference as read-only.
upstream_dependency.consumption_boundary: This package begins where Meridian_Master ends — after the Builder has generated a playable greybox city. Gameplay_Master assumes that city exists; it does not generate, describe, or validate world geometry itself.

architectural_scope.scope_enforcement_rule: Every framework file in this package defines interfaces, schemas, contracts, registries, lifecycle events, and extension points only. Where a concept touches an out-of-scope area (e.g. an ability's activation contract could theoretically include combat), this package defines the generic contract and explicitly stops short of any combat-specific implementation, damage model, or AI response — those belong to later, separate packages that will implement against this foundation's contracts.
architectural_scope.violation_handling: Any future addition to this package that introduces out-of-scope content (a named weapon, a specific mission trigger, dialogue text, an NPC's behavior tree) should be treated as a scope violation requiring removal, not as an acceptable expansion.

gameplay_manifest.role: Extension-point contract for future gameplay packages.

gameplay_rules.role: Architectural governance rules for this package and its consumers.

gameplay_schema.role: Consolidated JSON Schema definitions for every framework file below.

consumption_model.consumed_by: Future gameplay packages (Combat, AI, Missions, Dialogue, Economy, Vehicles) — not the VOID World Builder.
consumption_model.contrast_with_meridian_master: Meridian_Master.json is read by the World Builder to generate geometry. Gameplay_Master.json is read by future gameplay-system engineers to know what interfaces already exist and must be implemented against, not extended arbitrarily.
consumption_model.extension_pattern: A future package (e.g. a Combat Package) references this package's stable IDs and contracts (e.g. AbilityFramework's activation lifecycle) the same way this package references Meridian_Master's district IDs — read-only, additive, never modifying the foundation it builds on.

canon_references.note: This package supports these canon-confirmed facts architecturally. It does not restate their narrative content — each is cited to its source of truth.

dual_player_identity.requirement: Player identity system must support exactly two selectable named identities.
dual_player_identity.source: Vol IV Ch. 7 Canon Lock — Kaevon and Veronica as the two selectable player identities.

echo_shift_ability.requirement: Ability system must support a traversal-class ability that temporarily removes the player from an external perception system.
echo_shift_ability.source: Vol II, Hub Upgrade — Echo Shift.

non_corporeal_companion.requirement: Character framework must support a character entity with no fixed physical form.
non_corporeal_companion.source: Vol II — Echo, 'a shifting geometry of light that never quite resolves into a shape.'

tracked_state_variables.requirement: Save framework must persist the six tracked state variables exactly as defined upstream, not reinvent them.
tracked_state_variables.source: GameplayGraph.json (Meridian_Master, locked) — nyx_status, mira_saved, memory_fragment_count, compassion_flags, riggs_redemption_complete, talis_extracted.

memory_fragment_progression.requirement: Progression system must support a citywide collectible-driven progression resource.

single_first_person_moment.requirement: Player framework's camera/control contract must support a mode switch capability, used exactly once in the confirmed campaign.
single_first_person_moment.source: Vol IV, 5.1 — first-person reserved exclusively for the Descent connective scene.

intended_ue5_systems.note: These are the UE5 systems this package's contracts are designed to be implemented against. Naming them is architectural scoping, not implementation — no Blueprint or C++ code appears anywhere in this package.

generation_pipeline.note: gameplay_manifest is imported last because it consolidates extension points exposed by every framework file above it — it cannot be meaningfully assembled first. Framework order below character_framework follows the dependency chain formalized in GameplayRules.json (character is the root; save is cross-cutting and depends on everything before it).

design_authority.role: Source-grounded design authority for this package, added retroactively — this manifest predates that document's creation. Every model below cross-references its section.
design_authority.precedence_rule: Where this package's existing content and Gameplay_Design_Master.md's status tags disagree, the Design Master's status tag governs. This applies most directly to progression_model.skill_ability_mechanism below.

gameplay_state_model.status: INFERRED — no canon source diagrams a state-transition model explicitly; this list synthesizes states each individually evidenced across confirmed missions.
gameplay_state_model.authoritative_detail: Gameplay_Design_Master.md Section 6 table (entry/exit conditions per state).

player_capability_model.status: CANON for the unlockable list items individually; INFERRED for the foundational list (required by every mission, never itemized as such in any single source).

interaction_model.flow: PLAYER -> INTERACTION -> TARGET -> SYSTEM RESPONSE -> WORLD STATE CHANGE
interaction_model.status: CANON for existence of every interaction type listed in InteractionFramework.json; INFERRED for the generic flow diagram itself.

persistence_model.status: CANON for the six tracked state variables and identity selection; INFERRED for the other two persist categories and both temporary-state items.

progression_model.source: Gameplay_Design_Master.md Section 9, Section 20 UDD-03 and UDD-06
progression_model.skill_ability_mechanism: UNDEFINED — IMPLEMENTATION DECISION REQUIRED. Canon confirms two specific unlock outcomes (non-lethal takedown, Absolution mod) but never confirms a general mechanism. SkillFramework.json's prerequisite-graph/skill-tree architecture is PROPOSED, not CANON — see that file's own design_status field.
progression_model.currency_as_resource: UNDEFINED — IMPLEMENTATION DECISION REQUIRED. No source describes credits as spendable on player capability. ProgressionFramework.json's ProgressionResourceRegistry correctly avoids currency framing; this note exists to prevent a future package from assuming otherwise.

highest_priority_open_item.topic: Spire Server Hub / Nyx boss encounter discrepancy
highest_priority_open_item.effect_on_this_package: AbilityFramework.json's echo_shift_reference_instance and ability_slot_system make no claim about Server Hub combat and should not be extended to imply one exists until this is resolved.

source_traceability.status_preservation_rule: No file in this package may present a PROPOSED or INFERRED design as if it were CANON. Where this audit found a violation of that rule (SkillFramework.json), it was corrected in place with an explicit status field, not silently left as-is or rewritten from scratch.
